title: PR #142: Idempotent Webhook Ingestion & Crash-Safe Lease Recovery

overview.tldr: Adds a PostgreSQL-backed idempotency lease table and wraps `/webhooks/:provider` so retried or duplicate provider callbacks are safely ignored while crashed in-flight workers can recover after lease expiry.
overview.global_context: External providers (Stripe, GitHub) POST events to `webhookRouter`, which previously forwarded every payload straight into `WebhookDispatcher` without tracking event IDs.
overview.before_state: Every POST to `/webhooks/:provider` executed `dispatchProviderWebhook` unconditionally, causing double-charges/duplicate side effects whenever a provider retried on timeout.
overview.after_state: `webhookRouter` atomically claims `(provider, event_id)` in `webhook_idempotency_keys` before dispatch, marks it `COMPLETED` on success, or releases the claim on error.

nodes.label: PostgresIdempotencyStore
nodes.role: Atomic INSERT ... ON CONFLICT claim & release

nodes.label: webhook_idempotency_keys (PG)
nodes.role: Composite PK + partial index on CLAIMED leases

steps.title: Define the idempotency table schema and TypeScript store contract
steps.why_now: GitHub sorted these last (`migrations/` and `services/idempotency/types.ts`), but seeing the two states (`CLAIMED`, `COMPLETED`) and `ClaimDecision` union first makes the store and route logic self-explanatory.
steps.explanation: Introduces the `webhook_idempotency_keys` table keyed by `(provider, event_id)` with a partial index on active leases, alongside the `IdempotencyStore` interface.

callouts.text: Notice `ClaimDecision` defines both `SKIP_ALREADY_PROCESSED` and `SKIP_IN_FLIGHT_OR_DONE` in `H008`, which leads to a mismatch in the unit test (`H001`).

hunk_notes.H005: SQL table + partial index on `lease_expires_at` where `status = 'CLAIMED'`.

steps.title: Implement atomic lease claim, completion, and release in PostgresIdempotencyStore
steps.why_now: With the schema and types clear, inspect the exact SQL conflict resolution and error handling where race conditions or duplicate processing could slip through.
steps.explanation: Uses a single `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE WHERE status = 'CLAIMED' AND lease_expires_at < NOW()` statement so only one worker wins either a fresh event or an expired stalled lease.

callouts.text: Silent fail-open in `catch` (`H007` L29-32): if PostgreSQL errors or times out, `claimOrSkip` returns `{ action: 'PROCESS' }`. Confirm whether billing/payment webhooks must fail-closed (HTTP 500 so Stripe retries) instead!

Clock-source mix (`H007` L14 vs L22): `lease_expires_at` is computed from app-server `Date.now()`, whereas expiry comparison uses DB `NOW()`. Skewed app clocks could shorten or lengthen the 60s lease.

steps.title: Wire PostgresIdempotencyStore into the DI container and /webhooks/:provider route
steps.why_now: Now that you trust what `claimOrSkip`, `markCompleted`, and `releaseClaim` do, verify how incoming HTTP requests invoke them around `webhookDispatcher.dispatch`.
steps.explanation: Extracts `eventId` from `x-webhook-id` or `req.body.id`, short-circuits non-`PROCESS` decisions with HTTP 200, and releases the claim in `catch` so transient downstream failures can be retried.

callouts.text: If `releaseClaim` itself throws during a DB outage inside the `catch` block (`H002` L23), the original dispatch error is masked. Should `releaseClaim` errors be logged and swallowed?

steps.title: Audit unit tests (and catch a mocked-SQL bug!)
steps.why_now: GitHub put `__tests__/webhook-dedup.test.ts` as File #1, where it looked reasonable—but reading it AFTER `store.ts` immediately exposes a bug in the AI-generated mock!
steps.explanation: Tests duplicate suppression and expired-lease takeover using a mocked `db.query`.

callouts.text: Broken/tautological test in `H001` L7-14: the mock returns `rows: [{ status: 'COMPLETED' }]`, so `res.rows.length > 0` in `store.ts` will actually return `{ action: 'PROCESS' }`, NOT `{ action: 'SKIP_ALREADY_PROCESSED' }` (and `store.ts` never even emits `SKIP_ALREADY_PROCESSED`!). This test would fail if run!

untested_gaps: Tests mock `db.query`, so the actual PostgreSQL `ON CONFLICT ... WHERE` SQL query is never executed against a real database.
No route-level test covering missing `eventId` (400), successful `markCompleted`, or `releaseClaim` on downstream failure.
